body.text: The Treasury has set the colony's return for the coming season at {param:amount}, over {param:months} months.

I am obliged to say plainly what this is and what it is not. It is not a bill. Nobody is coming to your door for coin you do not have. It is a figure, and at the end of {param:months} months the books will show whether the colony reached it.
I have your last returns in front of me and they are {perception:returns}. Draw from that what you will; I am not permitted to draw it for you.

You may accept, and the Crown will record that you undertook it. You may decline, and the Crown will record that too. I would not have you believe the second is the graver of the two, whatever the tone of the letter you are reading.
A man who undertakes a figure and misses it has told the Treasury something about his judgement. A man who declines has only told it something about his colony.
I have seen governors accept out of pride and spend the season watching a number they could not move. It is not an edifying spectacle from this end either.

tone.text: I have the Treasury's figure before me {choice}.

options.text: and am glad of a target to work to
and note that nobody asked what it cost to raise
and can scarcely read it for the others beside it
and have given it the attention it merits

options.label: undertake the figure
options.text: The colony will return {param:amount} inside {param:months} months. You may set it down in the book over my name{insert:hedge}.

options.label: decline the figure, plainly
options.text: I will not undertake it. The ground here returns what it returns, and I would rather tell you so now than have you learn it from the books in {param:months} months.

tone.hateful: Kindly send the next figure without the sermon attached.
